title: Signal enrichment and automated response playbook for error visibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add structured enrichment to traces/logs and build a prioritized dashboard + automated response playbook for common failure modes (timeouts, overloads, model errors, HTTP/gRPC codes). Goal is to reduce MTTI/MTTR by enabling deterministic triage steps, attach provenance to errors, and create metric-backed alert thresholds with suggested remediation actions.
background: We have multiple incidents where errors surface as generic "model error" or 5xx with no clear traceable cause. Current dashboards show counts and p95 latency but lack per-request context (model variant, kv_cache_hit, queue_time_ms, batch_size) and standardized classification across HTTP/gRPC/model stack. That increases cognitive load for on-call and delays rollbacks or fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks instrumented at runtime entry/exit to attach model_name, model_variant, request_route, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, queue_time_ms, kernel_selection_hint
Log/metrics pipeline ETL updated to normalize an "error_taxonomy" field with one of: timeout, overload, model_runtime_error, model_rpc_error, client_bad_request, infra_io_error
Grafana dashboard with top-10 error signatures, per-model failure-rate, p99/p95 latency broken down by route and model_variant
Alert rules for high-severity signatures with runbook links and automated remediation suggestions (route fallback, scale-up, model-revert)
Playbook doc with step-by-step triage for each taxonomy category and canned CLI commands to view hot traces and recent model logs
Performance impact of tracing enrichment validated to <5% p50 latency overhead under production traffic in staging canary
implementation_notes: Use OpenTelemetry SDK to add attributes on spans at the handler boundary; attributes keys must be snake_case and prefixed with rw_ (e.g., rw_model_name)
Add middleware that computes queue_time_ms and KV cache hit boolean at request dequeue time and attach to span and log event
Map HTTP 5xx and gRPC codes to taxonomy: e.g., 504->timeout, 429->overload, 500 with model_error tag->model_runtime_error; preserve raw code in rw_transport_code
Update log-enrichment lambda in metrics pipeline to parse span attributes and emit normalized error_taxonomy field to observability index (Loki/BigQuery) for dashboarding
Sampling: keep 100% sampling for error spans, dynamic 1-5% for successful requests, ensure head-based sampling doesn't drop key error attributes
Store enriched spans in existing tracing backend (Jaeger) but export flattened records into BigQuery for long-term analytics and to power dashboards
Dashboard panels should support quick-filter by rw_model_name, rw_model_variant, rw_route, and rw_deployment_pool
Add a tagging convention for 'auto_fallback_candidate' on errors where automatic fallback to cheaper model is safe (defined in model metadata service)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable enrichment for 100% of traffic in staging, validate attribute correctness and overhead
Phase 2 (canary): enable enrichment for 10% of production traffic with feature flag; monitor CPU/latency regressions and trace volume costs
Phase 3 (ramp): increase to 50% then 100% after two clean canary windows; run cost review and retention policy update
Phase 4: activate dashboard panels and alerting; notify on-call rotation and runbook owners, add to pager duty escalation paths
Fallback: feature flag off to remove enrichment immediately if latency or costs exceed SLOs
open_decisions: Whether to canonicalize taxonomy as a single enum field in all telemetry sources or keep per-tier mapping and normalize in the ETL
Retention window for enriched records in BigQuery vs raw spans in Jaeger (trade cost vs queryability)
Thresholds for automated remediation actions (scale-up vs route-fallback) and whether to make them global or route-specific
Sampling strategy for low-volume routes where errors are rare but critical for customers
risks_mitigations: Increased trace volume leading to cost spikes -> mitigation: aggressive sampling for successes and retention TTL for enriched records; budget alerting in billing dashboard
Attribute extraction could be inconsistent across language runtimes -> mitigation: provide shared instrumentation library and unit tests, include schema contract checks in CI
False positives in taxonomy mapping (mislabeling model errors as infra) -> mitigation: include raw_transport_code and raw_stack_snippet fields in analytics to allow retroactive reclassification
Automated remediation could cause cascading rollbacks -> mitigation: start with suggested automated actions (manual approval) for high-impact routes, enable automatic only for low-risk routes
